information_for_contributors: This grammar exists because VS Code's built-in html.tmLanguage.json only
embeds source.js for a <script> whose type is empty or a recognized
JavaScript mime type. Any other type — including every mycelium/* type
this project uses — falls through to that grammar's last branch, which
assigns the block source.unknown: no grammar, so no syntax highlighting
at all. This injects one extra rule ahead of that fallback, matched only
for type="mycelium/...", that embeds source.ts instead. The prefix test
is the same one src/script-hooks.ts and editor/language-plugin.ts use to
decide a block's language; if that prefix ever changes, this does too.
The injection targets text.html.derivative, not text.html.basic. VS Code
opens .html files with the grammar registered for the html language,
which is html-derivative.tmLanguage.json (scopeName text.html.derivative)
— confirmed by reading extensions/html/package.json's languages/grammars
contributions. That grammar reaches html.tmLanguage.json only through
{ include: 'text.html.basic#core-minus-invalid' }, a reference to one
repository rule, which does not push text.html.basic onto the scope
stack the way tokenizing a file whose own scopeName is text.html.basic
would. An injectionSelector of text.html.basic therefore never matches a
real .html buffer; verified by tokenizing a sample through the actual
vscode-textmate/vscode-oniguruma engine outside the editor.
